summary: Jerzy Kuryłowicz was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Lviv (~1920–1923) and under Antoine Meillet (~1923–1925), later holding posts at the University of Lviv (~1926–1946) and Jagiellonian University (~1948–1965).

Jessie Pons is a scholar in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University by 2011 and was attested as a Junior Professor at Ruhr University Bochum in 2019.
Jesung Woo works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania and held a post at Dongguk University (attested 2001–2003).
Jey Flick works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sheldon Pollock (attested 1984–2007) and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley.
Jian Deng works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied as a disciple under Weijue Shi and succeeded him in 2005.
Jian Ouyang worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under Renshan Yang (~1904–1911). He founded the China Institute of Inner Learning and served as its head (~1922–1943).

Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Nankai University and Harvard University, supervised by Tu Weiming, Robert M. Gimello, and Zhichao Chen, and later served as Professor at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).
Jianming Hu works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and held a researcher post at Komazawa University (attested 2015).
Jiaqi Wang worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He studied under Gongga Rinpoche as a disciple and is attested as a PhD student at Columbia University in 2026.

Jiayao An works in history, archaeology, and sinology. She studied under Su Bai (~1979–1982) and held a post at the Institute of Archaeology, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, beginning around 1982.

Jiegang Gu was a sinologist and historian who studied at Peking University (~1913–1920) under Taiyan Zhang and Hu Shih. He held posts at Peking University, Fudan University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Jien Abe specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973) and served as a professor at Meiji University until 2001.

Jifu Lan works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Tunghai University (~1965–1969) and held a research post at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, retiring in 2019.

Jigdal Dagchen Sakya was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and held a post at the University of Washington (~1960–1963).

Jigme Chhoeda works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, having studied at Druk Sangag Choeling and Tango monasteries under Dudjom Rinpoche and others. His posts include Drapoi Lopen at Dratshang Lhentshog and Dorji Lopen at the Central Monastic Body.
Jigme Pema Wangchen is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dzi Gar Khenpo Nor Yang, Drukpa Khenpo Ngawang Chödrak, and Mi-pham-bśad-sgrub-chos-kyi-ñin-byed-mchog.
Jigme Tenpai Nyima studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and he taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fo Guang University for an MA (attested 2013) under supervisor Yongdong Shi, and also studied under Hui Xian.
Jikai Fujiyoshi worked in Buddhist studies. He was a member at Kyoto University (attested 1967) and served as a professor at Rissho University.

Jikido Takasaki specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo and Savitribai Phule Pune University. He held positions at the University of Tokyo, Komazawa University, Osaka University, Waseda University, and served as President of Tsurumi Women's University.
